title: B8 scout: pin the Claude fresh-execute path, the Codex fix-delta path, _resume_compatible and run_claude's error shape so B8 v3 can name the session-resume mechanics
spec:
Read-only scout for B8 (Claude fix rounds resume the executor's session; held T-1509, v2 T-1587 got spec review T-1589 request_changes twice because the spec could not name the mechanics). Read goal/T-1403 (git show goal/T-1403:<path> or a worktree on that branch); change nothing. Answer each question with file:symbol facts (line numbers as a hint only).

Q1 Fresh execute path. In spawn.run_worker, list in order every step between the claim and run_claude for a fresh Claude execute task: ensure_worktree, bus.claim with wt, packet render, packet_meta (where session_id is stored), pool.reserve/release, the executor='claude:<tier>' write, skill telemetry, log_run (inside run_claude?), _combined_usage. For each, say whether it depends on the packet render.

Q2 Codex fix delta. How a Codex fix round reaches the executor today: the executor.reply / _exhausted path, how the daemon dispatches a fix round (_dispatch_reply_worker, _dispatch_fresh_fix: what each passes), whether the delta is the fix task's own spec (bus.get(fix id)['spec']) or something the daemon passes, and which symbol makes a Codex fix round reuse the parent's worktree and branch (the reason its commits land on task/<parent>).

Q3 _resume_compatible(parent): what it verifies, its callers, and what happens when it returns False.

Q4 run_claude: its return shape on success and on error (where stderr / the error message lives; whether 'No conversation found' or a missing-session error is observable distinctly from other errors and in which field); whether run_claude accepts a resume/session argument today; where it calls log_run and with which outcome.

Q5 Registry and concurrency: how worker_registry / worker_control record a running worker per task (keys), so a resume plan can tell whether a given session's task has a live worker.

Q6 Tests: in tests/test_spawn.py and tests/test_executor.py (and tests/test_daemon.py for fix-round dispatch), the fixtures and patch targets existing tests use for run_claude, ensure_worktree, executor.reply and the registry, so a spec can name the same seams.

Post via bus_post_result: summary (<= 1500 tokens), findings list of {q, fact, path, symbol, line, confidence}, provenance 'repo'. Any confidence < 0.7 must say what is uncertain.
acceptance: result.findings answers Q1-Q6, each with at least one path and symbol
every finding has a confidence; any below 0.7 names what is uncertain
provenance is ['repo'] and no file in the repo changed

result.summary:
Posted the Q1–Q6 answers to T-1618 as done, all from `goal/T-1403`, and no repo file changed. The first post errored, probably for length, so I posted a shorter version.

The main thing for B8: `goal/T-1403` already has Claude resume mechanics. The spec should extend them, not add new seams.

- **Q1:** The order is pick account, write `executor='claude:<tier>'`, `packet()`, `render('execute')`, `packet_meta`, skill exposure, `pool.reserve`, `ensure_worktree`, `bus.claim`, then `run_claude`. Only the executor write is independent of the packet render. `session_id` goes into `packet_meta.session_id` inside `run_claude`, after the CLI returns. `log_run` is also called inside `run_claude`.
- **Q2:** The daemon tick sets the fix task's `worktree` and `branch` to the parent's when the plan is resume. That is why Codex fix commits land on `task/<parent>`. The delta comes from `_fix_round_delta` (failures plus filtered acceptance), not from the fix task's own spec. `_dispatch_fresh_fix` is the one that renders the fix spec, on a new `task/<fix>` branch.
- **Q3:** `_resume_compatible` checks that the worktree exists, is clean, and that HEAD descends from `codex_thread_head`. Its only caller is `resume_plan`. When it returns False, the plan is fresh with reason `incompatible_worktree`. `resume_plan` already returns fresh for any non-Codex parent, so Claude parents always plan fresh today.
- **Q4:**
  - **Resume support:** `run_claude` already accepts `resume_session`. `run_worker(resume_task=, resume_prompt=, session_id=)` and `spawn.resume_worker` call it.
  - **Missing session:** a missing-session error is not special-cased. It only shows up in the `reason` string of a failed result, or in `output.result`, so detection needs a substring check.
  - **Unverified:** I did not run the CLI, so I don't know its exact error wording (that finding is at 0.5 confidence).
- **Q5:** There is one registry JSON per task, and a worker is live if its status is not in {cancelled, done, fail

goal/T-1403 already has a Claude resume path: run_claude(resume_session=), run_worker(resume_task, resume_prompt, session_id), spawn.resume_worker. Codex-only resume_plan/_resume_compatible decide fix-round mode; a Claude parent always plans fresh today. No file changed.

findings.fact: run_worker fresh execute order: pool.pick -> executor='claude:<tier>' bus.update -> packet() -> render('execute') -> packet_meta -> _shadow_tool_disclosure + skill exposure (bus.update packet_meta) -> pool.reserve -> ensure_worktree -> bus.claim(task,'claude:<acct>',wt) -> bus.update(account) -> run_claude. Only the executor write is independent of render; packet_meta/skill telemetry/allowlist derive from it. session_id is stored by run_claude into packet_meta.session_id after CLI returns. log_run is inside run_claude. _combined_usage used only in tool-escalation rerun and resume_output.

daemon tick (fix_round_for): executor.resume_plan; mode resume -> bus.update(fix, worktree=parent.worktree, branch=parent.branch or task/<parent>) (this is why commits land on task/<parent>), then spawn_async(_dispatch_reply_worker, fix, parent, _fix_round_delta(parent,fix), plan). Delta is daemon-built (failures from parent resume_hint or rejecting reviews + filtered fix acceptance), not the fix spec. reply() sets _run_task_id=fix, re-checks plan (mismatch -> incompatible), runs codex 'resume <thread> <delta>' in parent worktree; _state_target routes state to fix, rounds to parent. incompatible -> _dispatch_fresh_fix(worktree=None, branch=task/<fix>, packet+render('execute') from fix spec, _dispatch_worker). _exhausted is the fresh Claude fallback, not the fix path.

_resume_compatible(task)->(bool,reason): False if no worktree; True if no codex_thread_head (legacy); False if git status dirty; else head must descend from recorded head. Sole caller resume_plan (executor.py:329); False -> {'mode':'fresh','reason':'incompatible_worktree'}. resume_plan also fresh for no codex_thread, rounds>=MAX_ROUNDS, executor provider != codex.

run_claude has kw resume_session (adds --resume id --tools '' empty mcp, log_run no-op) and task['_resume_session'] (--resume with normal tools). Returns {'status':'done','output':json} on success; {'status':'failed','output':out,'reason':'budget or error exit (rc=N): '+result[:500]} on error exit; non-JSON -> reason 'non-JSON output (rc=N): '+(stdout+stderr)[-500:]; timeout/held/superseded variants. 'No conversation found' is not special-cased anywhere; detect by substring on reason or output.result. log_run outcome done|error (rc), plus rate_limit/no_cli, with session_id.
Uncertain: actual CLI wording/stream of a missing-session error not verified.

worker_registry keeps STATE/workers/<task_id>.json with fields role, model, provider, account, pid, thread, worktree, branch, started_at, last_event_at, status, status_reason, epoch, tools, parent, tokens, usd. get(task) -> doc; live = status not in TERMINAL {cancelled,done,failed,held}; reconcile(alive_fn) marks dead pids failed. session_id is not a registry field (lives in task packet_meta.session_id), so map session->task via bus then registry.get. worker_control.launch_epoch/is_current/write_if_current guard superseded launches. resume_worker reuses recorded account/model/tools.

test_spawn: FakePopen + patch spawn.subprocess.Popen, spawn.shutil.which, spawn.worker_registry, spawn.trust_workspace, spawn.secrets_for_role, spawn.env_policy.worker_env; run_worker tests patch spawn.run_claude and spawn.ensure_worktree (or pre-mkdir TMP/'wt'/id). test_executor: patch.object(executor,'resume_plan'/'_resume_compatible', return_value=(True,'compatible')), executor.reply(parent,'repair',fix_round_task_id=..., plan=...), P.Executor rows. test_daemon: self.swap(executor,'reply'/'_resume_compatible'), daemon._dispatch_fresh_fix(tid,reason), patch daemon.worker_registry get/reconcile.

open_questions: Reuse run_worker(resume_task=)/resume_worker or add a new fix-round path?
Exact CLI text for a missing --resume session
suggested_next: Extend resume_plan for claude parents via packet_meta.session_id, falling back to _dispatch_fresh_fix
